dossier.public_summary: The dip looks different for odd vs even events and changes dramatically from sector to sector, with only a couple of deep dips dominating the signal. This pattern is expected for a background eclipsing binary leaking into the aperture, not a 2.1 Earth-radius planet on the target.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits have a different depth, strongly favoring a binary at twice the period (12.9d signal is the primary of a 25.8d EB). In a planet both should be identical.

Depth changes dramatically between sectors and within the same pipeline, from 1723 ppm in sector 25 to 130 ppm in sector 53. A planet on target should be steady; a blend / EB with different aperture contamination produces exactly this.

reasons.why: Individual transits are highly inconsistent and the signal lives in only a few deep events (1898 ppm epoch 59, 1723 ppm epoch -57). This is noise/blend behavior, not a stable planetary transit.
